estates.naive-yearly:
[Naiveyearly.com](https://naiveyearly.com) is a traveling gathering for the web.

It brings designers, developers, artists, educators, writers, organizers, and other curious people into the same room to explore the web as a medium and material.

Talks take the form of personal essays, performances, and experiments. Just as much attention is given to the conversations between them. Rather than looking back nostalgically or forward to technological utopias, Naive Yearly is interested in what the web makes possible in the present.

Gatherings

2027 — Athens, Greece, at Castor Place
2024 — Ljubljana, Slovenia, at the Museum of Architecture and Design
2023 — Copenhagen, Denmark, at the National Film School of Denmark

Publication

All talks are published on [naive-yearly.are.na](https://naive-yearly.are.na/), extending the gathering and its conversations onto the web.

Made in collaboration with [Hypertext Foundation](https://hypertext.foundation), [Are.na](https://are.na), and many others.
estates.diagram-website:
[Diagram.website](https://diagram.website) is an internet map which also serves as my curatorial landscape. It features 200+ links to different internet philosophies and movements. The feeling I'm trying to provoke is that of the starry night in a remote area because sometimes it is hard to see the depth and scale of the universe when caught inside an urban environment, or in the case of the internet, when we are stuck inside social media.

I believe handmade maps offer an intriguing alternative to navigate space. They are not trying to make a 1:1 representation of reality, but to recall walks that are eithter important or worthy - and to share them with others.

Made in collaboration with [Elliott Cost](https://elliott.computer/).
estates.naive-weekly:
[Naiveweekly.com](https://www.naiveweekly.com/) is a living archive of the Poetic Web.

It documents the sites, books, people, and places that make up an emerging internet culture rooted in care and curiosity for the web. Through interviews, observations, and collected links, Naive Weekly traces the people and ideas shaping how we live with the internet.

The project began in 2018 as a Sunday email with links to the quiet, odd, and poetic web. Today, it has grown into an independent publication and an ever-expanding archive of internet culture.

Available on the web, through RSS, and as an infrequent newsletter.

Edited by Kristoffer Tjalve. Designed with [Elliott Cost](https://elliott.computer/), with a logo by [Benedikt J. Scheckenbach](https://dreams-tm.co/).
estates.tiny-awards:
[Tinyawards.net](https://tinyawards.net/) is an annual celebration of the small, poetic, creative, handmade web.

Founded in 2023, the Tiny Awards recognize personal, non-commercial websites that might otherwise be overlooked by more traditional awards. They celebrate people making things for the web out of curiosity, imagination, and the simple pleasure of making something.

Each year, anyone can nominate a website created in the previous twelve months. A selection committee chooses a shortlist, and the wider internet votes for its favourite. The winner receives a small cash prize and a handmade trophy, created by a different artist each year.

Past winners

2026 — Cursor Camp, by Neal Agarwal. A multiplayer summer camp for cursors, full of games, toys, and unexpected encounters.
2025 — Fifty Thousand Names, by Leo Scarin. A digital memorial to Palestinians killed in Gaza, giving individual names and lives a place beyond the headlines.
2024 — One Minute Park, by Elliott Cost. A collection of one-minute visits to parks and green spaces around the world.
2023 — Rotating Sandwiches, by Lauren Walker. A website dedicated to photographs of sandwiches, slowly rotating.

Organized with [Matt Klein](https://kleinkleinklein.com/) and [Matt Muir](https://webcurios.co.uk/).
estates.my-girlfriend-is-an-artist:
[Mygirlfriendisanartist.com](https://Mygirlfriendisanartist.com) is a personal love project. On every refresh, the website features a different of her horizontal photographs combined with a short text written by me. The site was made as a birthday gift and prioritises our shared memories.

My girlfriend, [Ana Šantl](http://iamnotana.com/)'s analogue photographs are the visual aspiration for all of my work with the internet. Her photographs bring a soft tenderness to any subject, a calm invitation to perceive the world differently.
estates.wilderness-land:
[Wilderness.land](https://wilderness.land) is a website to I made to look like a PokémonGo map with links to hundreds of websites hidden in the cells using Google Sheet. The site is an invitation to get lost on the internet and a reminder that we can repurpose productivity tools made by giants to serve ourselves and our community.

Published in 2022.
estates.internet-phone-book:
[Internetphonebook.net](https://internetphonebook.net) is a printed publication for exploring the vast poetic web.

It brings together hundreds of personal websites alongside essays and observations about the web as a medium for creative expression. Issue One, published in 2025, features more than 700 websites by designers, developers, artists, writers, curators, educators, and other internet people.

At its heart, the Internet Phone Book is about connecting people. Each website is listed with its own telephone number, which readers can dial using [Dial-a-Site](https://internetphonebook.net/dial/) to visit the site and meet the person behind it. The book is a low-tech invitation to discover the web through its inhabitants.

Issue One

The first issue was printed twice and sold out twice. It has since found its way into libraries, bookshops, and collections around the world, including the National Library of Greece, the National Library of Scotland, and the British Film Institute Library.

Beyond the book

The Internet Phone Book has also become a reason to gather. Through exhibitions, talks, readings, and other events in cities including Athens, Rotterdam, Copenhagen, Seoul, Amsterdam, and London, the publication creates opportunities for people to meet and exchange ideas about the web.

Issue Two

The next edition is in development.

Made in collaboration with [Elliott Cost](https://elliott.computer/).
estates.url-poetry-club:
[URL Poetry Club](https://urlpoetry.club) is an attempt at writing found poems using domain names. The project reflects on how we discover and memorize the sites we love, and how kinship is formed online.

Request

I'd like to evolve the site into a workshop format where the participants write poems as an act of care and liberation. Maybe you know where I could host such a workshop? Email: poetry@cloudlord.management
estates.apossible: [Apossible.com](https://apossible.com/) is an investigation of what makes human thrive. With Andrew Trousdale, Jake Dow-Smith and Bryan Wolff.

about.owner: Kristoffer Tjalve is the owner-operator of Cloudlord.management, an internet surreal estate holding company. He works as an independent organizer from his studio in Athens, Greece. He is dedicated to the web as a medium, material, and philosophy, and works across formats, from websites to awards, conferences, and printed publications. His practice is centered around nurturing environments where emerging practitioners and narratives flourish to keep the web spirit alive.
